blocks.h2: Does Your McHenry Basement Need an Overhead Sewer?

tiles.body: The floor drain rises in heavy rain or high water and goes back down after.
No sag, roots or break, and it still happens.
Or you're about to finish one.

tiles.h3: You Live Near the River or Lakes
tiles.body: Saturated ground puts more water into the system.

blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer System Works
blocks.body: With an overhead sewer, the basement no longer drains to the sewer by gravity. Floor drains and basement fixtures empty into a sealed pit. An [ejector pump](/mchenry/ejector-pump) lifts the water up to a line near the ceiling, a check valve keeps it from flowing back and it leaves the house above the level the sewer can reach. If the sewer backs up, there's no low opening for the water to come through.

blocks.intro: Overhead sewers protect basements from what happens in the public sewer.

items.h3: High Water Near the Fox River
items.body: When the river and the ground are high, as in July 2017, sewer systems carry more water than usual. Gravity floor drains are the first place it shows up.
About 4 in 10 McHenry homes went up between 1990 and 2009, and a finished basement raises the stakes. An overhead system protects every drain down there.
We camera your line before recommending a conversion. If a sag or break is the cause, a [sewer repair](/mchenry/sewer-repair) may be enough.

blocks.h2: Overhead Sewer Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Will an overhead sewer keep my basement dry in a flood?
items.preview: It stops sewer backups. Groundwater and surface water need other fixes.
items.answer: It stops sewer water from backing up through basement drains. Groundwater coming through walls needs a [sump pump](/mchenry/sump-pumps), and surface floodwater needs grading and sealing.

items.q: I already have an ejector pump for a basement bathroom. Can it be used?
items.answer: Sometimes. If the existing pit and pump are big enough for the whole basement, they may become part of the system.

items.q: How long does it take to install?
items.answer: Usually a few days, depending on the basement layout and fixtures.

items.q: Do I still need a sump pump?
items.preview: Yes, if groundwater gets in. They do different jobs.
items.answer: Yes. An overhead sewer handles sewage. A sump pump handles groundwater. Many McHenry basements need both.

items.q: How much does an overhead sewer system cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on your basement. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on sewer depth, basement layout, fixtures and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
